source: Rowland, Bates & DeLosh (2014) On the reliability of retrieval-induced forgetting, Experiment 1
finding: Direct replication of Anderson et al. 1994 Exp 2 with undergraduates. RIF replicated, but as a small effect.
numbers: Exp 1 N=72: Nrp .45 vs Rp- .41, t(71)=2.59, p=.01, d=0.31; Rp+ .79. Simonsohn small-telescopes d33% = 0.26, so counted as a success.
limits: Category-cued recall allows output interference. The original effect size could not be computed from the 1994 paper.
agent_relevance: Expect a small effect (d about 0.3) even in the best-known paradigm. A lesson that suppresses siblings costs little per item.

source: Rowland, Bates & DeLosh (2014) Experiment 2, internet sample
finding: RIF replicated in a more diverse online sample with a shortened design.
numbers: Exp 2 N=140 MTurk, 4 lists, 5 min distractor: Rp- .42 vs Nrp .50, t(139)=4.51, d=0.38; Rp+ .63. Original d33%=0.26.
limits: Shorter lists and delay than the original. Recall was typed.
agent_relevance: RIF is not an artefact of the student lab sample. It survives short delays and fewer items.

source: Rowland, Bates & DeLosh (2014) Experiment 3, independent cue procedure
finding: Failed to replicate the cue-independent RIF test of Anderson & Spellman (1995). Cue independence is the key evidence for inhibition over interference.
numbers: Exp 3 N=67: Rp- .56 vs Nrp-similar .52, t(66)=0.92, p=.36; cue-independent effect d=-0.05, 95% CI [-0.36, 0.27]. Original d33%=0.21. Rated uninformative, not a refutation.
limits: Small N for the effect size. The CI includes both 0 and the small-telescope effect.
agent_relevance: The strongest evidence for true inhibition is the least replicated. Do not build the agent on a claim that siblings are inhibited in a cue-free way.

source: Murayama, Miyatsu, Buchli & Storm (2014) Forgetting as a consequence of retrieval: a meta-analytic review of retrieval-induced forgetting
finding: First major meta-analysis. Results largely supported inhibition accounts but gave some challenging evidence, and results varied with how RIF was measured.
numbers: Abstract only, read through the Europe PMC record. No effect sizes captured this session.
quote: The results largely supported inhibition accounts but also provided some challenging evidence
limits: Abstract only. The full text was blocked by bot protection. Loprinzi 2026 cites it as showing RIF is robust across materials, paradigms and populations.
agent_relevance: Robustness is high, but the inhibition-versus-interference verdict depends on the test used.

source: Oliva & Storm (2022) Examining the effect size and duration of retrieval-induced facilitation
finding: The opposite sign: retrieval can help related items when material is integrated and the test is delayed. The replication found it about half as large as the original.
numbers: Meta-analysis k=12 experiments, n 24 to 35 each, fixed effect 0.05 (SE .01), 95% CI [.03,.07]. Overall 4% (CI 2 to 6%) vs 7 to 11% in Chan (2009) and Chan et al. (2006). No effect of delay (1 day, 1 week, 2 weeks). I2 negative, read as 0% heterogeneity.
quote: the size of the effect was found to be somewhat smaller than previously observed
limits: Small samples. Facilitation needs integrated materials. The effect is a few percent.
agent_relevance: Siblings can gain, not only lose, if the lessons are woven into one structure. Integration is the design lever.

source: Loprinzi, Shopeju & Storm (2026) Temporal effects of exercise on retrieval-induced forgetting
finding: Large replication. Classic RIF replicated. The earlier claim that exercise preserves RIF across two tests did not.
numbers: N=372 in 5 groups (71 to 77 each). First test Rp- minus Nrp- from -.051 to -.077 (Group 1: .354 vs .431). Second test -.030 to -.054 (Group 2: .419 vs .449). RIF shrank at the second test in all groups, driven by better recall of Rp- items.
limits: Intervention null. Shrinking is attributed to repeated testing.
agent_relevance: Suppression fades after a second recall attempt. A later pass that retests siblings can restore them.

source: Loprinzi, Shopeju & Storm (2023) Acute exercise on memory: application of the RIF paradigm
finding: Three experiments on acute exercise: no effect on RIF when exercise came before study, but exercise between two recall tests seemed to preserve RIF. The 2026 study (b06) did not confirm this.
numbers: Exp 1 N=180 (control 60, moderate 57, vigorous 63), recognition test: no effect. Exp 2 N=225, cued recall: no effect. Exp 3 N=158: exercise preserved RIF across two tests.
limits: Abstract only. The Exp 3 finding was not reproduced at N=372.
agent_relevance: A moderator found at N=158 failed at N=372. Treat small moderator effects with doubt.

source: Reanalysis and failure to replicate Wimber et al. (2015): Does inhibition cause forgetting after selective retrieval? (Cortex 2018)
finding: Reanalysis of an fMRI study claiming targeted inhibition. The key interaction depended on coding missing responses as errors. Two behavioural replications found no forgetting at all.
numbers: Original forgetting p<.01; interaction p=.041. With missing trials removed or set to chance, no reliable difference. Two replications: no forgetting.
quote: we failed to find any forgetting at all
limits: Abstract read in full. One paradigm variant (picture forced-choice recognition).
agent_relevance: Neural evidence for inhibition is fragile to coding choices. Missing data in an agent's logs can fake a suppression effect.

source: Raaijmakers & Jakab (2016) On testing the strength independence assumption in retrieval-induced forgetting
finding: A non-inhibitory SAM model simulation shows that the lack of correlation between Rp+ gain and Rp- loss, used as evidence for inhibition, is not a valid test.
numbers: Large-scale simulations with a simplified SAM model. A noninhibitory model is not likely to predict a significant correlation across subjects even when the probabilities are correlated.
limits: Abstract only. A modelling paper, not new human data.
agent_relevance: The no-correlation argument for inhibition is weak. Do not use it to justify designs.

source: Explaining retrieval-induced forgetting: a change in mental context between study and restudy is not sufficient to cause forgetting (2016)
finding: Rival theory (Jonker, MacLeod & Seli 2013): RIF arises because practice shifts mental context and people search the wrong context. This paper tried to replicate the restudy-with-context-shift effect and reports that context change alone did not cause forgetting.
numbers: Abstract only. No numbers captured.
limits: Abstract only. Loprinzi 2026 still cites the context account as live.
agent_relevance: A rival explanation says the effect is context search, which is cheap to control: keep lessons in one context.

source: Relearning can eliminate the effect of retrieval-induced forgetting (Psychological Research 2022)
finding: Restudy of non-retrieved items after practice removes RIF, even after three rounds of retrieval practice. Fits a temporary accessibility reduction.
numbers: Two experiments. RIF eliminated by restudy, also after three practice rounds. No further numbers captured.
limits: Abstract only. Earlier work disagreed on restudy.
agent_relevance: A cheap repair: re-present siblings after a lesson is applied.

source: Reward eliminates retrieval-induced forgetting (PNAS 2014)
finding: A reward for correct retrieval practice removed RIF. The no-reward condition showed it. Authors suggest spreading activation within the category.
numbers: RIF in the no-reward group, none in the reward group (apple juice vs beep). Numbers not captured.
limits: Abstract only. Small samples, single lab.
agent_relevance: A positive outcome signal during practice may protect unpracticed siblings.

source: Retrieval-practice task affects relationship between working memory capacity and retrieval-induced forgetting (Memory 2016)
finding: The link between working memory capacity (and stop-signal speed) and RIF depends on task type: it appears with within-list retrieval, not with extra-list generation.
numbers: Four experiments (WMC in Exp 1 to 3, SSRT in Exp 4). Significant correlations only for within-list practice.
limits: Abstract only. Individual-difference links are task specific.
agent_relevance: Whether suppression happens depends on how retrieval is done, so lesson lookup design matters.

source: Medial prefrontal cortex stimulation reduces retrieval-induced forgetting via fronto-parietal beta desynchronization (J Neurosci 2024)
finding: Stimulating medial PFC raised accuracy on competitors and reduced RIF. Target accuracy was unchanged. Fits an inhibitory control role.
numbers: N=50 (27 male, 23 female), real vs sham. Beta desynchronisation in left DLPFC under 500 ms. Effect size not captured.
limits: Abstract only. Small sample for a stimulation effect.
agent_relevance: Suppression is tied to control machinery. An LLM has no matching module, so the analogy is loose.

source: Everything you ever wanted to know about the Think/No-Think task, but forgot to ask (Behav Res Methods 2024)
finding: Methods guide for suppression-induced forgetting, the sibling paradigm to RIF. People must actually attempt stopping. Informative precues strengthen forgetting. Double-cue designs separate inhibition from interference.
numbers: Hanslmayr 2010: stronger forgetting with an informative precue. Wang 2015 double cue: interference gave cue-specific impairment, direct suppression generalised to an independent cue.
quote: People must try to stop retrieval
limits: Guide with no pooled effect. Notes that participants may do the opposite of instructions.
agent_relevance: Suppression needs an active stop goal. An agent that never tries to stop recall is unlikely to show it.

source: Stramaccia et al. (2020) meta-analysis of suppression-induced forgetting (JEP General)
finding: Search summary only: small to moderate pooled suppression-induced forgetting in healthy people.
numbers: Summary figure: 0.28, 95% CI [0.14, 0.43].
limits: Not opened. The figure comes from a search snippet and the PDF link did not return a PDF.
agent_relevance: Think/No-Think forgetting is about as large as RIF.

source: Anderson, Bjork & Bjork (1994) Remembering can cause forgetting: retrieval dynamics in long-term memory
finding: Founding study: practising some category items impairs unpracticed items from the same category compared with items from unpracticed categories.
numbers: No numbers verified. Rowland 2014 says the original effect size could not be computed and gives Exp 2 n=36.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: The source of the warning in our schema: practise one lesson, lose its siblings.

source: Loftus & Palmer (1974) Reconstruction of automobile destruction
finding: Verb wording in a leading question changed speed estimates and later reports of broken glass.
numbers: From memory, not verified: 'smashed' about 40.8 mph vs 'contacted' about 31.8 mph.
limits: Not opened. Numbers from recall.
agent_relevance: Wording of a question can alter what is recalled. An agent that rereads its own notes is open to the same effect.

source: What Fifty Years of Research on the Misinformation Effect Can Tell Us: A Meta-Analytic Review (2026 preprint)
finding: Largest synthesis of the three-phase misinformation paradigm, 1975 to 2025. The effect is real and very uneven. Warnings after the misinformation reduce it.
numbers: 480 studies, 1,998 effect sizes, N=59,079. Average g=0.694, 95% CI [0.259, 1.128]. Heterogeneity sigma2=0.697, I2=92.21%. Post-event testing not a significant moderator. Control accuracy positively linked to effect size.
limits: Preprint. Abstract read only; moderator sizes not captured.
agent_relevance: A late warning helps. Add a check that flags suspect inputs after they were read.

source: Meta-analysis: implanting rich autobiographical false memories (2023)
finding: 30 studies: implanting rich autobiographical false memories has a large, generalisable mean effect.
numbers: Lower limit of the 80% credibility value d=1.13 (abstract).
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Source credibility and repetition can plant false items.

source: A meta-analysis of correction effects in science-relevant misinformation (Nature Human Behaviour 2023)
finding: Corrections of science misinformation on average did not work well.
numbers: 205 effect sizes from 74 reports, N=60,861. d=0.19, P=0.131, 95% CI -0.06 to 0.43.
limits: Abstract only. Not a memory-paradigm study.
agent_relevance: Telling the agent a note is wrong does not remove its pull.

source: Bypassing versus correcting misinformation: efficacy and fundamental processes (J Exp Psychol General 2025)
finding: Six preregistered experiments: giving a competing belief changes attitudes more than a plain negation, unless attitudes were already formed on first exposure.
numbers: Six preregistered experiments. Numbers not captured.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Replace a wrong item with a better one rather than only deleting it.

source: Chattaraj & Raj (2026) Transformers Remember First, Forget Last: dual-process interference in LLMs
finding: 39 LLMs. Retroactive interference (old values lost after updates) versus proactive interference (new values blocked by old ones). This is not retrieval-induced forgetting.
numbers: Proactive degradation greater than retroactive in 39/39 models, d=1.73. RI and PI scores correlate weakly, r=0.21 (CI -0.11 to 0.49). Size predicts RI resistance, R2=0.491. Top size tier 171.2 vs 142.8.
quote: hallucination rates remain below 1% in both conditions
limits: Different paradigm (key-value updates). Mitigations not tested.
agent_relevance: Early information intrudes on later answers, so lesson order matters.

source: Chattaraj & Raj (2026) reasoning models and error types
finding: Reasoning models resist retroactive interference but not proactive. RI errors are retrieval failures. PI errors are intrusions of older values from the same category.
numbers: Reasoning models RIES 178.0 (SD 12.6) vs 150.3 (SD 18.2), d=1.76. o1: RIES 186.4 vs PIES 22.0 (8.5x gap). Claude-4.5-opus 178.4 vs 170.3. 5,409 RI and 9,753 PI errors: RI retrieval failure 50.8%; PI same-key intrusion 56.1%; hallucination 0.9% (RI), 0.2% (PI). Accuracy at 300 updates 24.6% (96.0% at 50).
limits: Single synthetic paradigm.
agent_relevance: Failures are mix-ups of real items, so verify against the source list instead of hunting for invention.

source: Li & Wang (2026) Retrieval-Induced Forgetting in LLMs: A Reproducible Failure Mode and a Verified Fix (ICML 2026)
finding: Elaborating on one of several related items in context lowers later recall of the others, as in human RIF. A one-turn post-hoc prompt to list every item restores recall.
numbers: Qwen-2.5-7B drop 11.2 pp (judge-scored, N=150, p<1e-6). Qwen-2.5-72B drop 24.9 pp. Post-hoc list prompt: 100% recovery on 7B, 98% on 72B. The same text before elaboration: about half at 7B, harmful at 72B (98% vs -5%, a 103 pp gap). Late-layer attention to target tokens fell to 0.42x baseline. Masking elaboration positions cut recovery 21%.
limits: One model family, two sizes. Page summary only; the full paper was not seen. Judge-scored.
agent_relevance: Directly tests our warning. The fix is to re-list all siblings after any deep dive on one.

source: Chan et al. (2024) Conversational AI powered by large language models amplifies false memories in witness interviews
finding: An LLM chatbot asking misleading questions made people form more false memories of a crime video. Here the AI is the source of misinformation, not the subject.
numbers: N=200, four groups, five misleading questions each. Generative chatbot: over 3 times the control false memories and 1.7 times the survey. 36.4% of chatbot users' responses were misled. Level held and confidence stayed higher after one week.
limits: Abstract-level numbers. Human subjects.
agent_relevance: LLM output can corrupt other memories. Notes written by one agent may mislead another.

source: Cao et al. (2023) Retentive or Forgetful? Diving into the knowledge memorizing mechanism of language models
finding: Controlled experiments on LM forgetting: vanilla models forget, pre-training makes models retentive, and knowledge relevance and diversification affect memory formation.
numbers: Qualitative in abstract. No figures captured.
limits: No numbers seen.
agent_relevance: Related knowledge helps retention. This mirrors facilitation when items are integrated.

source: Resurrected memories: sleep-dependent memory consolidation saves memories from competition induced by retrieval practice (Psychon Bull Rev 2021)
finding: Retrieval practice helped temporally close pairmates and hurt temporally far unrelated pairmates. It hurt far but related pairmates without sleep and helped them after sleep.
numbers: Exp 1: practice accuracy 74.4% (SD .21) round 1, 85.7% (SD .20) round 2. Adjacent unrelated, short delay: non-target .67 vs control .62. Far unrelated: -.07. Four-way interaction F(2,140)=3.78, p=.025, partial eta2=.051. Adjacent trial-type effect F(1,70)=40.86, partial eta2=.37.
quote: sleep extends the benefits of testing to related information
limits: Word-scene pairs, not category exemplars. Sleep was compared across experiments.
agent_relevance: Proximity and a consolidation gap turn harm into help. A delayed review step might help.
